concept.technique_name: definitional clue matching for equivalent word pairs

examples.problem_statement: Select the two answer choices that, when used to complete the sentence, fit the meaning of the sentence as a whole and produce completed sentences that are alike in meaning. Mr. Hirsch says he will aim to preserve the foundation's support of ______ thinkers, individuals who are going against the trends in a field or an acknowledged set of opinions.

solution.operation: Read the clause after the comma as the definition of the blank: "individuals who are going against the trends in a field or an acknowledged set of opinions"
solution.result: The blank must be filled by words meaning "opposed to established trends or opinions"
solution.description: Treat the appositive following the comma as a built-in definition of the type of thinkers being described, so the sentence tells you outright what meaning the blank needs.

solution.operation: Match that required meaning against "iconoclastic" and "heterodox"
solution.result: Both describe people whose opinions run counter to established norms
solution.description: Check the two candidates that carry the required sense; because both describe opinions running counter to established norms, they satisfy the definition and are also alike in meaning as the format demands.

solution.operation: Test "doctrinaire" and "dogmatic" against the required meaning
solution.result: Both mean the opposite: adhering to established principles
solution.description: Eliminate this pair by noting that adhering to established principles is the reverse of going against them, so they contradict the definition given after the comma.

solution.operation: Test "integrative" and "synthesizing" against the required meaning
solution.result: Both refer to a willingness to bring together disparate points of view
solution.description: Eliminate this pair as well: bringing together disparate viewpoints is a different idea from opposing prevailing ones, so neither fits the defined sense.

examples.answer: Choice A: iconoclastic; AND Choice D: heterodox

key_reminders: An appositive phrase set off by a comma often defines the blank outright.
In Sentence Equivalence the two correct choices must both fit the sentence and be alike in meaning.
Wrong pairs frequently cluster as opposites or as an unrelated but internally matched pair.
common_mistakes: Picking the doctrinaire/dogmatic pair because they form a matched pair, ignoring that they mean the opposite of going against established opinion.
Picking integrative/synthesizing on the strength of their pairing alone, though bringing viewpoints together is not opposing them.

examples.problem_statement: Choose the better version of the underlined portion; choice (A) repeats the original sentence. The recent string of burglaries, in addition to poor building maintenance, have inspired the outspoken resident to call a tenants' meeting. (A) The recent string of burglaries, in addition to poor building maintenance, have  (B) Recently, the string of burglaries, along with the poor building maintenance, has

solution.operation: Strike out the middleman modifier "in addition to poor building maintenance"
solution.result: The recent string of burglaries ... have inspired the outspoken resident
solution.description: Remove the interrupting phrase that sits between the subject and the verb; such modifiers never change the number of the subject, and cutting them makes the true pairing visible.

solution.operation: Identify the subject of the stripped sentence
solution.result: The subject is string, which is singular
solution.description: With the middleman gone, read off the head noun that actually governs the verb: it is string, not burglaries, and string is singular.

solution.operation: Apply subject-verb agreement in number to string
solution.result: The singular has is correct, so have is wrong
solution.description: Because subject and verb must agree in number, a singular subject requires the singular verb form, which rules out the plural have of the original.

solution.operation: Select the choice that supplies the singular verb
solution.description: Pick the option whose verb matches the singular subject identified in the previous step.

key_reminders: Eliminate the middlemen: modifiers between subject and verb do not affect agreement.
Phrases like "in addition to" or "along with" do not make a singular subject plural.
Subject and verb must agree in number.
common_mistakes: Taking the nearby plural burglaries as the subject and accepting the plural have.
Treating "in addition to poor building maintenance" as a compound subject that pluralizes string.

examples.problem_statement: Select one entry for each blank from the corresponding column of choices, filling all blanks in the way that best completes the text. The setting in which the concert took place (i) ______ : the group's performance was elegant and polished, but the sound, which seeped across the cold, unresonant high school auditorium, was oddly (ii) ______ , given the energy the players seemed to be putting into it. Blank (i): A exacted a toll, B encouraged nervousness, C solved a dilemma. Blank (ii): D clangorous, E tepid, F inviting.

solution.operation: Read the "but" as a contrast between the performance and the sound
solution.result: The performance is positive ("elegant and polished"), so Blank (ii) must be negative
solution.description: Use the contrast conjunction to set the required charge of the second blank: since the first half of the contrast is praise, the description of the sound has to run the other way.

solution.operation: Add the second condition from "given the energy the players seemed to be putting into it"
solution.result: The sound must also contrast with the apparent energy of the performers
solution.description: Layer on the closing clause, which demands not just any negative word but one that clashes with visible energy, tightening what Blank (ii) can accept.

solution.operation: Screen the Blank (ii) choices against both conditions
solution.result: Only "tepid" meets them, so it is correct
solution.description: Apply the two conditions together to the second column and keep the single word that satisfies both.

solution.operation: Read the sentence as a whole to fix Blank (i)
solution.result: The setting had a negative effect on the performance, so "exacted a toll" fits best
solution.description: Now that the sound is established as disappointing, ask what the setting did to the performance overall and choose the phrase carrying that negative effect.

solution.operation: Test the rival Blank (i) choice "encouraged nervousness"
solution.result: Rejected: the sentence never discusses the psychological state of the musicians or audience
solution.description: Check the other negative-sounding option and discard it, because being negative is not enough when the sentence gives no support for a claim about anyone's nerves.

examples.answer: Choice A: exacted a toll; AND Choice E: tepid

key_reminders: A "but" between two descriptions fixes the polarity of the second one.
Every condition the sentence supplies must be satisfied, not just the polarity.
A choice with the right charge is still wrong if the sentence provides no support for its specific content.
common_mistakes: Choosing "clangorous" because it is negative, though a clangorous sound would not contrast with the players' energy.
Choosing "encouraged nervousness" for Blank (i) on negativity alone, when the sentence says nothing about psychological state.

examples.problem_statement: Select one entry for each blank from the corresponding column of choices, filling all blanks in the way that best completes the text. The government has no choice but to (i) ______ the incessant demands for land reform, and yet any governmental action that initiated land reform without requisite attention to agrarian reform would (ii) ______ the overall goal of economic modernization. Blank (i): A anticipate, B heed, C silence. Blank (ii): D delineate, E condone, F compromise.

solution.operation: Read "and yet" as signalling a negative consequence for the stated "overall goal"
solution.result: Blank (ii) needs a word meaning to damage that goal, and only "compromise" fits
solution.description: Use the contrast marker to see that acting without attention to agrarian reform harms the modernization goal, then take the only choice in the second column that expresses such harm.

solution.operation: Use the same "and yet" to constrain Blank (i)
solution.result: The government's response must be in line with initiating land reform, so "silence" is incorrect
solution.description: Note that the contrast only makes sense if the government is moving toward reform, which eliminates a word meaning to suppress the demands.

solution.operation: Weigh the description of the demands as "incessant"
solution.result: The demands already exist, so "anticipate" is incorrect
solution.description: Read the adjective attached to the demands: something already unceasing cannot be anticipated, so that choice contradicts the sentence.
With the other two options ruled out, confirm that the survivor actually names a fitting response to existing demands.

examples.answer: Choice B: heed; Choice F: compromise

key_reminders: "And yet" marks a contrast, so the second clause must cut against the first.
Adjectives attached to the blank's object (here "incessant") carry hard constraints.
Fill the blank that the sentence constrains most tightly first, then use it to settle the other.
common_mistakes: Choosing "silence" for Blank (i), which breaks the contrast the "and yet" sets up.
Choosing "anticipate" despite "incessant" telling you the demands are already ongoing.
